summary: Proposed hyperscale data centre campus on around 88 ha of Hunterston Estate farmland beside the former Hunterston A/B nuclear power stations, north of West Kilbride, promoted by Eneus Energy with Revera Energy (both Carlyle-linked). An EIA scoping request (26/00138/EIA) was submitted to North Ayrshire Council on 25 February 2026 and a scoping opinion was agreed on 30 March 2026; a full application with EIA is expected in 2026. Scoping material describes multiple buildings with a combined footprint of up to 300,000 m2 and heights up to 35 m, construction from 2027 for around seven years. The developer has not published a MW capacity; campaigners infer at least 500 MW. A separate consented BESS at Hunterston (Revera, 400 MW/800 MWh, FID June 2026) shares the grid node.
maturity_explanation: EIA scoping request 26/00138/EIA validated 27 Feb 2026 and scoping opinion agreed 30 Mar 2026 on the North Ayrshire portal; no PAN or planning application located as of 30 Jul 2026, and the council has publicly confirmed no formal application is under consideration. Developer states an application is expected in 2026.
anticipated_operational_date: Phased; completion of all works expected 2034 (scoping report, as reported)

latest_development.headline: North Ayrshire Council issues EIA scoping opinion (Scoping Agreed) for the Hunterston data centre; full application with EIA expected later in 2026

unknowns: IT load / grid import capacity in MW — not disclosed by the developer; APRS's 'at least 500MW' is a campaign inference
Which corporate entity will be the applicant (Eneus Energy Limited SC739030, a holdings entity, or a project SPV); scoping applicant field shows only consultant Tetra Tech

Exact red-line boundary and which field parcels of the Hunterston Estate are included; hence exact agricultural land classification per parcel (Grade 3 reported by APRS, not yet verified against the scoping report or James Hutton Institute mapping)

Whether and how the site boundary overlaps or adjoins the consented Hunterston BESS (450 MW consent reported by APRS in 2022 vs Revera's 400 MW/800 MWh FID scheme) and the shared 400 kV connection arrangements
Grid connection agreement details (TEC quantity, connection date) for the data centre itself
Operational job numbers — developer says 'currently under review'
Formal positions of Fairlie and West Kilbride community councils and of statutory consultees beyond the scoping responses
Any Peel Ports / Clydeport involvement (the data centre is on Hunterston Estate land, not Peel's Hunterston PARC, but interface with PARC infrastructure is unclear)
